children: Volkswagen (VOW) shares climbed about 3% on Friday after the automaker secured board backing for a broad cost-reduction program that includes another 50,000 job cuts and a smaller vehicle portfolio.

The measures would bring planned workforce reductions across the group to roughly 100,000. Volkswagen also intends to cut its model range by half by 2035 and simplify vehicle configurations, changes designed to lower operating complexity and better match production with demand.

The company is also reassessing the role of four German facilities in Emden, Zwickau, Hanover and Neckarsulm, where future vehicle production remains uncertain. Volkswagen has said European manufacturing capacity exceeds demand by more than 500,000 vehicles annually.

The restructuring comes as the automaker deals with U.S. tariffs, weaker Chinese demand and growing pressure from lower-cost Chinese manufacturers. First-half operating profit fell 11.6% year over year to 5.9 billion euros, while operating margin declined to 3.8%.
What it means for the stock: Investors appear to view the restructuring as a potential path toward lower costs and improved profitability, though execution remains a key risk.

title: Volkswagen Stock Jumps on 50,000 Job Cuts
